summary: gc --all-merged now lists branches by prefix (refs/heads/, refs/remotes/origin/; plain gc harness/ and harness-merge/) and runs every pass, deleting merged spec/x, docs/y, flat etc. A second bug found by the check: a refused `branch -d` (no upstream, HEAD behind origin/main) ended gc under set -e; act now prints `! failed: <argv>` and gc goes on. L4 plan written.
verified_how: RED first: 306/308 (both new checks failed: --all-merged deleted only flat; plain gc died on harness/z's refused -d). GREEN: bash tests/run.sh 309/309 and lib/check.sh 309/309; bash -n bin/harness tests/run.sh; scratch repro in the scratch dir shows dry-run prints each would: once.

dead_ends.why: branch -d measures against upstream or HEAD; the suite's $T/proj main is behind origin/main, so -d refused every fixture branch

discoveries.text: git 2.43 here: `git worktree remove` (no --force) removes a clean worktree whose only extra files are ignored (.next/ via .gitignore or info/exclude). R9's refusal had another cause (an undeletable file, or the loop dying under set -e); the fallback chain is the fix. `git worktree list` sorts worktrees by path (main first), so fixtures can fix the order by name.

cmd_gc's act no longer exits non-zero on a failed command: it prints `! failed: <argv>` and returns 0, so `act git worktree remove` failures no longer end gc either (L4-02 replaces that call with its own fallback and `! could not remove` line). $T/proj's local main is behind origin/main in the suite, so `branch -d` of a branch with no upstream is refused there.
Plan fixes L4-04's failure fixture: a `git` wrapper first on PATH for one runner that fails `-C <dir> fetch -q --prune origin` (only gc runs that argv); no STUB_GC_FAIL in production code.

questions: D1 default (decisions/2026-10-25-gc-all-merged): gc keeps `branch -d`, so a merged branch with no upstream in a checkout whose main is behind origin/main stays locally (`! failed:` line; its origin copy goes). Would you rather gc delete it with `git update-ref -d refs/heads/<b> <sha>` after its origin/main check (as safe, never refused)?
